name: Can door frames be widened for wheelchair or accessibility needs?

mainEntity.name: Can door frames be widened for wheelchair or accessibility needs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Door frames can be modified to wider dimensions to enhance accessibility, provided the surrounding wall structure allows it. For hallways and bathrooms, widening a standard door opening to 32 or 36 inches accommodates wheelchairs and walkers. Because altering the width requires removing king and jack studs and installing a wider structural header, your contractor must determine whether the wall is load-bearing before cutting. Drywall patching, baseboard adjustments, and new finish carpentry are then completed to blend the modified opening into the room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, frames can be widened for accessibility, but the wall framing and header must be structurally rebuilt, followed by drywall and finish trim repairs.
